'''Ishii Shrine''' (石井神社) is a [[Shinto shrine]] located in [[Niigata Prefecture|Niigata Prefecture]], [[Mishima District (Niigata)|Mishima District]], [[Izumozaki, Niigata|Izumozaki Town]], Ishiimachi. It is a {{ill|Shikinaisha|ja|式内社}} {{ill|Disputed shrine|ja|論社|lt=candidate}}. The shrine is regarded as the total shrine of Izumozaki Town. Its former Rank under the {{ill|Modern system of ranked Shinto shrines|en|Modern system of ranked Shinto shrines|lt=Modern system of Ranked Shinto shrines}} was {{ill|Village shrine|ja|村社}}.

== Overview ==
The founding date of the shrine is unknown. According to legend, during the {{ill|Age of the gods (Japanese mythology)|ja|神代}}, {{ill|Ōkuninushi|ja|大国主命}}, who sought to pacify {{ill|Sado Island|en|Sado Island|qid=Q998623|lt=Sado Island}}, sprinkled water from a stone well, causing twelve sacred trees to grow overnight. These trees were used to construct a ship to cross to Sado. A great deity of maritime protection was enshrined at the site of these sacred trees, known as Iibana. For this reason, the shrine was originally called {{ill|Jūnisho Shrine|ja|十二所神社}}. During the {{ill|Nara period|en|Nara period|qid=Q189178|lt=Nara period}}, prayers by the {{ill|Sado bugyō|en|Sado bugyō|qid=Q4274645|lt=Sado governor}} calmed a storm, enabling safe return. This increased faith in the shrine, which was relocated from {{ill|Mt. Jūni|ja|十二山}} in Kanazawa Village to its current site in 712 CE (Wadō 4).<ref name="Izumozaki Hoketsu">{{Cite news |title=Izumozaki: Hoketsu Materials |newspaper=Sato Bookstore |date=1906-09-01 |author=Nishizawa Shinji (ed.) |page=}}</ref>

== deity ==
{{ill|Ōkuninushi|ja|大国主命}}

== Auxiliary Shrines ==
* {{ill|Sumiyoshi Shrine|en|Sumiyoshi Shrine|qid=Q32512|lt=Sumiyoshi Shrine}} ({{ill|Auxiliary shrine|ja|Keigai-Sessha}})

== Festivals ==
Since 1690 CE (Genroku 3), the shrine has held the {{ill|Maritime Safety Prayer Festival|ja|海上安全祈願祭}} on June 17–18. Later, this was conducted jointly with other shrines, and in 2010 (Heisei 22), it was renamed the {{ill|Izumozaki Grand Festival|ja|出雲崎大祭}}. A mikoshi procession visits Ryōkandō, Anase, Iibana, and returns to Ryōkandō.

== Visitor Information ==
'''Access'''
* Rail: From {{ill|East Japan Railway Company|en|East Japan Railway Company|qid=Q499071|lt=JR East}} [[Izumozaki Station]], [[Kashiwazaki Station]], or [[Nagaoka Station]], take the {{ill|Echigo Kotsu|en|Echigo Kotsu|qid=Q11636491|lt=Echigo Kotsu}} bus bound for Izumozaki Garage and alight at "Ryōkandō-mae" bus stop.

{{nihongo|'''Iwai Shrine'''|石井神社 (出雲崎町)}} is a [[shinto shrine]] in the [[Engishiki Jinmyōchō]]. It is located in [[Echigo Province]].

'''Ishii Shrine''' (いわいじんじゃ) is a {{ill|Shinto shrine|abstract|Q845945|ar|جينجا|arz|ضريح شنتو|bcl|Shinto shrine|ca|Jinja|cs|Šintoistická svatyně|da|Shinto-tempel|de|Shintō-Schrein|el|Σιντοϊστικό Ιερό|eo|Ŝintoa sanktejo|es|Jinja|eu|Jinja|fa|معبد شینتویی|fi|Šintolainen pyhäkkö|fr|Sanctuaire shinto|hi|शिंतो मंदिर|hr|Šintoistički hram|hu|Sintó szentély|id|Jinja|it|Jinja|ja|神社|ka|ძინძია|ko|신사 (신토)|lb|Shintō-Schräin|mr|शिंतो मंदिर|nl|Jinja (heiligdom)|no|Jinja|or|ଜିଞ୍ଜା|pl|Jinja|pt|Templo xintoísta|ru|Дзиндзя|sc|Jinja|simple|Shinto shrine|sl|Šintoistično svetišče|sr|Шинтоистички храм|sv|Jinja|th|ศาลเจ้าชินโต|tok|tomo sewi pi nasin sewi Sinto|tr|Şinto tapınağı|uk|Святилище (синто)|uz|Dzindzya|vi|Thần xã|wuu|神社|zh|神社|zh_yue|神社|qid=Q845945}} in Ishii-chō, {{ill|Izumozaki|Q1204583|qid=Q1204583}}, {{ill|Santō District, Niigata|Q1155567|qid=Q1155567|lt=Mishima District}}, {{ill|Niigata Prefecture|Q132705|qid=Q132705}}. It is a {{ill|Shikinaisha|fr|Shikinaisha|zh|式內社|qid=Q134917286|lt=Shikinaisha}} {{ill|Shikinai Ronsha|ja|論社|qid=Q135022904}}. It is the sōsha of {{ill|Izumozaki|Q1204583|qid=Q1204583}}. Under the {{ill|Q712534|lt=modern shrine ranking system}}, its former rank was {{ill|Son-sha|Q134917284|qid=Q134917284}}.

=== Overview ===
The founding date is unknown. In the {{ill|Age of the Gods|Q70447980|qid=Q70447980|lt=Age of the Gods}}, when Ōkuninushi-no-Mikoto sought to pacify {{ill|Sado Island|Q998623|qid=Q998623|lt=Sado}}, he sprinkled water from a stone well and built a ship overnight from twelve sacred trees that grew at once, then crossed to Sado. At that time, a great sea-protecting deity was enshrined at Ihana, where those twelve sacred trees stood. For that reason, it was originally called Jūnisho Shrine. In the {{ill|Nara period|Q189178|qid=Q189178}}, the {{ill|Sado bugyō|Q4274645|qid=Q4274645}} prayed there and was able to return safely after a storm subsided; devotion deepened, and in {{ill|Wadō (era)|Q1373026|qid=Q1373026}} 4 ({{ill|712|Q23521|qid=Q23521}}), the shrine was moved from Jūniyama in Ihana, Kanazawa Village, to its present site.<ref name="出雲崎北越資料">{{Cite news |title=出雲崎：北越資料 |newspaper=Sato Bookstore |date=1906-09-01 |author=Compiled by Nishizawa Shinji |page=}}</ref>

=== Festivals ===
From {{ill|Genroku|Q1325001|qid=Q1325001}} 3 ({{ill|1690|Q7678|qid=Q7678}}), it has been held on June 17 and June 18 as the “Maritime Safety Prayer Festival.” Later it came to be held jointly with other shrines, and from {{ill|Heisei era|Q234510|qid=Q234510}} 22 it was renamed the “Izumozaki Grand Festival.” The mikoshi goes from Ryōkandō around Amase and Ihana and returns to Ryōkandō.

=== Local information ===
'''Access'''
* Rail: from {{ill|Izumozaki Station|Q6102426|qid=Q6102426}}, {{ill|Kashiwazaki Station|Q5353481|qid=Q5353481}}, or {{ill|Nagaoka Station|Q1138252|qid=Q1138252}} on {{ill|East Japan Railway Company|Q499071|qid=Q499071}}, take {{ill|Echigo Kotsu|Q11636491|qid=Q11636491}} bound for Izumozaki depot, get off at “Ryōkandō-mae”
